summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, PTSD, bipolar disorder, and prior abdominal surgeries was admitted for a recurrent incarcerated incisional hernia causing severe pain, nausea, and vomiting. He underwent successful open repair with mesh placement. Postoperatively, he developed mild atelectasis and leukocytosis, both managed conservatively. The incision showed blanching erythema, prompting a course of oral cephalexin, but no signs of active infection. He progressed well on pain control, diet advancement, and ambulation. By discharge, he was afebrile, tolerating a regular diabetic diet, ambulating independently, and had adequate pain control on oral medications. He was discharged home with instructions on wound care, activity restrictions, and follow-up with his surgeon and PCP.
